artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Gather Up (2021) is a career-spanning compilation by British musician Matt Berry, released on Acid Jazz Records. The album collects 21 tracks drawn from his prolific decade with the label, showcasing his evolution as a singular voice in rock and experimental pop. Musically, Gather Up highlights Berry’s eclectic style—blending psychedelic rock, baroque pop, and vintage British folk with lush arrangements, dramatic vocals, and a penchant for the theatrical. The collection features both fan favorites and rare non-album tracks, including the iconic "Snuff Box Theme," offering a comprehensive overview of his adventurous sonic palette.

As a retrospective, Gather Up serves as both an introduction for new listeners and a celebration for longtime fans, capturing the breadth and depth of Berry’s work over ten years. The album is notable for its expert curation by Berry himself, emphasizing his role as a genuine musical maverick and sonic explorer. While not a traditional studio release, Gather Up received positive attention for its cohesive presentation and the quality of its selections, reinforcing Berry’s reputation as a distinctive and influential figure in contemporary British rock.
